name: WALLACE.DEV
summary: An evolving portfolio designed to present real projects, technical growth and inspectable evidence without inventing experience.
problem: Present student-level technical work professionally without relying on fake experience, arbitrary skill scores or generic portfolio claims.
solution: A responsive evidence-based portfolio that connects skills to projects, documents project status, and separates completed evidence from future work.
next: Production testing, final CV/domain integration and deployment verification
target: Employers, clients, collaborators and reviewers who need a clear view of Wallace’s real work and current development level.
goals: Communicate identity and current level honestly
Show real project evidence
Make project progress easy to inspect
Remain maintainable as more projects are built
research: The project has evolved through repeated portfolio reviews, responsive design work and a deliberate shift from a long static page toward evidence-based project presentation.
implemented: Dedicated project index and project detail pages
Server-backed contact form with PostgreSQL storage, admin inbox and email notifications
challenges: Replace percentages and unsupported claims with statuses, project links and inspectable evidence.
Move detailed case studies into dedicated pages while keeping the homepage concise.
Generate responsive WebP variants and load below-the-fold images lazily.
lessons: A portfolio should grow with projects rather than endlessly adding decorative sections.
Accessibility and performance need to be designed into components, not added at the end.
future: Connect a production domain and update canonical/sitemap metadata
Add the final CV when supplied
Run production Lighthouse and browser testing
Replace remaining placeholders with project-specific screenshots where available

name: Remote Income Match™
alt: Remote Income Match current project preview
summary: An active project exploring a more systematic way to help people evaluate remote-income opportunities. Only verified implementation evidence is presented as completed.
problem: The project is centered on the difficulty of evaluating remote-income opportunities that fit a person’s situation. The exact product requirements are still being refined during development.
solution: A matching-oriented product concept. Specific routes, data sources and matching behavior remain marked as in development until they are implemented and tested.
next: Verify implemented features, add testing evidence and publish a repository when ready
target: People evaluating remote-income opportunities; exact target-user segments are still being refined.
goals: Turn the product concept into a working, testable system
Document only implemented functionality
Create clear evidence for matching logic and user flows as they are built
research: Research and requirements work are in progress. The portfolio intentionally does not claim a completed matching engine, live opportunity database or verified results yet.
challenges: Planned functionality is separated from implemented evidence.
Keep the case study updateable as the product definition becomes more precise.
lessons: Product claims should follow implementation evidence.
A development status can be informative without using arbitrary completion percentages.
future: Document verified target users and requirements
Add architecture after implementation decisions are real
Publish GitHub/live links only when they exist

name: Expense Tracker
summary: A completed interface design prepared for future implementation. Development, database behavior and results are intentionally not claimed yet.
problem: The real problem statement from the project brief still needs to be documented before implementation.
solution: The interface design is complete. The implementation approach will be documented when development starts.
target: Target users have not yet been verified in the portfolio documentation.
goals: Preserve the completed design
Document the real requirements
Turn the design into a working application in traceable stages
research: Research evidence has not yet been supplied. Add only research actually performed.
challenges: The case study explicitly marks software development and testing as upcoming.
lessons: A strong design is evidence of planning, but it is not evidence of a working application.
future: Add verified problem statement and target users

name: Hospital Management System
alt: Hospital Management System interface design preview

problem: The exact system problem and requirements need to be documented from the original design brief before development.
solution: A completed interface concept that can be converted into a working information system after requirements are verified.
next: Verify requirements and begin system implementation
target: Intended users and operational roles must be verified from the project brief before being published.
goals: Document the real workflow and requirements
Translate the interface into a maintainable system
Add database and testing evidence after implementation
research: No verified research record has been supplied for publication yet.
challenges: The page does not claim patient, billing, appointment or records modules unless they are actually implemented.
lessons: Information-system case studies need workflow and data evidence, not just screenshots.

name: Mobile App

problem: The app’s verified problem statement has not yet been added to the portfolio documentation.
solution: A completed interface design that provides a starting point for future mobile implementation.
next: Document the app purpose/user flow and choose implementation technology
target: Target users still need to be documented from the real project brief.

Document navigation/user flow
Build and test the app after technology selection

name: Database System
summary: A database-oriented project at the design stage. Schema, queries, constraints and database-engine claims will be added only when verified from the implementation.
problem: The exact data problem and entity requirements still need to be documented from the real project brief.
solution: A completed design stage prepared for implementation and later evidence such as an ER diagram, schema and tested queries.
next: Document entities/relationships and begin database implementation
target: The system’s real users and data owners need to be documented before publication.
goals: Document the database purpose
Create verified entity/relationship evidence
Implement constraints and queries
Test data integrity
research: Verified data-requirement research has not yet been supplied.
challenges: The page does not claim tables, keys or queries that have not been verified.
lessons: Database evidence should include schema, relationships, constraints and tested queries—not just an interface.
